acid-strength.def: How fully an acid gives up its proton, measured by Ka. An acid is stronger when its conjugate base is more stable: the negative charge spread by resonance, pulled by electronegative atoms, or held on a large atom.

oxyacid.def: An acid in which the acidic H is bonded to an O that is bonded to a central atom (H–O–X), such as HOCl or HNO₃. More O atoms or a more electronegative central atom makes it stronger.

organic-acid-base.def: A carboxylic acid (–COOH) is a weak acid whose conjugate base, the carboxylate (–COO⁻), is stabilized by resonance. An amine (–NH₂) is a weak base that accepts a proton on its nitrogen lone pair.
